{{short description|Mathematical constant}}
The '''Erdős–Tenenbaum–Ford constant''' is a [[mathematical constant]] that appears in [[number theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|
first1=Florian|last1=Luca|first2=Carl|last2=Pomerance|author2-link=Carl Pomerance|title=On the range of Carmichael's universal-exponent function|journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]]|volume=162|year=2014|issue=3|pages=289–308|mr=3173026|doi=10.4064/aa162-3-6|url=https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/rangeoflambda13.pdf}}</ref> Named after mathematicians [[Paul Erdős]], [[Gérald Tenenbaum]], and [[Kevin Ford (mathematician)|Kevin Ford]], it is defined as
:<math>\delta := 1 - \frac{1 + \log \log 2}{\log 2} = 0.0860713320\dots</math>
where <math>\log</math> is the [[natural logarithm]].

Following up on earlier work by Tenenbaum, Ford used this constant in analyzing the number <math>H(x,y,z)</math> of integers that are at most <math>x</math> and that have a divisor in the range <math>[y,z]</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Tenenbaum|first=G.|authorlink=Gérald Tenenbaum|issue=2|journal=[[Compositio Mathematica]]|language=French|mr=739737|pages=243–263|title=Sur la probabilité qu'un entier possède un diviseur dans un intervalle donné|url=https://www.numdam.org/item?id=CM_1984__51_2_243_0|volume=51|year=1984}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Ford|first=Kevin|authorlink=Kevin Ford (mathematician)|doi=10.4007/annals.2008.168.367|issue=2|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|mr=2434882|pages=367–433|series=Second Series|title=The distribution of integers with a divisor in a given interval|volume=168|year=2008|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0401223}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Koukoulopoulos|first=Dimitris|arxiv=0905.0163|doi=10.1093/imrn/rnq045|issue=24|journal=[[International Mathematics Research Notices]]|mr=2739805|pages=4585–4627|title=Divisors of shifted primes|year=2010|volume=2010|s2cid=7503281}}</ref>

== Multiplication table problem ==

For each positive integer <math>N</math>, let <math>M(N)</math> be the number of distinct integers in an <math>N \times N</math> [[multiplication table]]. In 1960,<ref>{{cite journal|first=Paul|last=Erdős|authorlink=Paul Erdős|title=An asymptotic inequality in the theory of numbers|journal=Vestnik Leningrad. Univ.|volume=15|year=1960|pages=41–49|mr=0126424}}</ref> Erdős studied the [[asymptotic]] behavior of <math>M(N)</math> and proved that
:<math>M(N) = \frac{N^2}{(\log N)^{\delta + o(1)}},</math>
as <math>N \to +\infty</math>.

Tenenbaum improved the Erdős multiplication table estimate, and Ford established an asymptotic best bound.
